Heartflow is a medical technology company advancing the diagnosis and management of coronary artery disease, the #1 cause of death worldwide, using cutting-edge technology. The flagship product—an AI-driven, non-invasive cardiac test supported by the ACC/AHA Chest Pain Guidelines called the Heartflow FFRCT Analysis—provides a color-coded, 3D model of a patient’s coronary arteries indicating the impact blockages have on blood flow to the heart. Heartflow is the first AI-driven non-invasive integrated heart care solution across the CCTA pathway that helps clinicians identify stenoses in the coronary arteries (RoadMap™Analysis), assess coronary blood flow (FFRCT Analysis), and characterize and quantify coronary atherosclerosis (Plaque Analysis). Our pipeline of products is growing and so is our team; join us in helping to revolutionize precision heartcare.

Heartflow is a publicly traded company (HTFL) that has received international recognition for exceptional strides in healthcare innovation, is supported by medical societies around the world, cleared for use in the US, UK, Europe, Japan and Canada, and has been used for more than 750,000 patients worldwide.

Location: San Francisco, CA (In-Person)

Duration: 10–12 Weeks (Summer 2027)

About The Role

We are seeking a highly motivated Platform Engineering Intern to join our team in-person at our San Francisco office for the Summer 2027 term. This 10-to-12-week program is designed to provide you with hands-on, high-impact experience building and scaling cloud infrastructure within a regulated medical device environment.

Working directly alongside our senior platform engineers, you will help support and optimize the foundational systems that power Heartflow’s cloud-based, AI-driven products. This is not a shadowing role; you will actively contribute to our codebase, streamline our software delivery, and tackle real-world engineering challenges.

A Path to Your Future: We are looking for candidates who are seeking a full-time role in the following year (e.g., graduating in late 2027 or Spring 2028). Our ultimate goal, based on demonstrated performance and budget availability, is to convert successful interns into full-time Platform Engineers upon graduation.

What You Will Do



- Cloud Infrastructure: Gain practical, hands-on experience building, scaling, and maintaining secure cloud infrastructure.
- Infrastructure as Code (IaC): Write, review, and deploy infrastructure configurations to ensure scalable and repeatable environments.
- CI/CD Pipelines: Design, optimize, and maintain Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment pipelines to streamline the software delivery process.
- Container Orchestration: Work with modern containerization technologies to deploy and manage microservices effectively.
- Developer Tooling: Identify bottlenecks and improve internal developer tools to enhance engineering productivity across the organization.
- Capstone Project: Own a dedicated, high-impact summer project from end to end. You will architect a solution, implement it, and formally present your findings and deliverables to the broader engineering team at the conclusion of the program.

What We Are Looking For



- Target Graduation Date: Currently pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field, with an expected graduation date that aligns with seeking a full-time role in the following year (2028).
- Foundational Knowledge: A strong understanding of core computer science principles, software engineering fundamentals, and cloud computing concepts.
- Technical Curiosity: Familiarity with or a strong desire to learn Infrastructure as Code, CI/CD practices, Linux systems, and container orchestration (e.g., Docker, Kubernetes).
- Motivation & Drive: Highly motivated self-starter who thrives in a collaborative, fast-paced environment and is eager to learn from senior engineers.
- Communication Skills: Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to articulate technical concepts and present project findings effectively.

What We Offer



- Direct Mentorship: 1:1 guidance and daily collaboration with experienced senior platform engineers.
- Real-World Impact: Your work will directly support products that utilize AI to revolutionize cardiovascular care.
- Career Growth: A structured pathway with the potential for a full-time return offer upon graduation.
- Vibrant Environment: An engaging, in-person collaborative experience at our San Francisco headquarters.

A reasonable hourly rate estimate for this internship is $45 to $60.

role: Synthetic Data for Edge AI System Engineer Intern
jd:
Job Description

Change the world. Love your job.

At TI, Systems engineers focus deeply on understanding the technical needs, and future trends of an industry or end equipment, then create new products and innovative forward-looking product roadmaps to solve them. Systems Engineers are an integral part each phase of new product development at TI. In the early stages of product development, systems engineers interface with key stakeholders (customer decision-makers, application engineers, marketing, management, sales, IC design engineers, technology development) to negotiate specifications, perform trade-offs, understand the competitive landscape, and ultimately develop detailed technical definitions for new products. They then collaborate with the full IC development team (design, applications, test, product engineers) to deliver products to the market which are compelling, competitive, cost-conscious, manufacturable, and importantly, successful in growing TI’s business.

We are seeking a highly motivated PhD student to join our Embedded AI team in Kilby Labs this summer to work on synthetic data generation and augmentation for edge AI on resource-constrained microcontrollers. Limited availability of high-quality training data is one of the biggest barriers to adopting edge AI, and you will help us find and evaluate better ways to address it. As a key member of our team, you will survey the state of the art, develop and test new techniques, and rigorously evaluate how well they work on real-world data and on embedded hardware.

In this systems engineering intern role, you’ll have the chance to:



-  Research and develop synthetic data generation and augmentation techniques that address data scarcity for edge AI on resource-constrained microcontrollers 
-  Survey the state of the art and identify the most promising approaches for your problem 
-  Work with time-series sensor data from a variety of applications, supporting both classification and regression tasks 
-  Design and run rigorous experiments to evaluate whether synthetic data improves model performance on real-world data 
-  Evaluate techniques under embedded hardware constraints, including low-precision quantization 
-  Analyze the quality, coverage and usefulness of generated data 
-  Collaborate with internal research, software and application teams 
-  Document findings and present results, trade-offs and recommendations to technical and business stakeholders 

Qualifications

Minimum Requirements:



-  Currently pursuing a PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field, with research focused on machine learning, signal processing, or embedded AI 
-  Cumulative 3.0/4.0 GPA or higher 

Preferred Qualifications



-  Solid background in machine learning for time-series data and signal processing 
-  Research experience in synthetic data generation, data augmentation, generative models (e.g., GANs, diffusion models, TimeGAN), or learning from limited and imbalanced data, ideally demonstrated by publications 
-  Experience with sensor signal analysis (e.g., vibration, motor/line current, PIR, spectral and time-frequency analysis) and an interest in fault detection and predictive maintenance 
-  Strong programming skills in Python, with deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow 
-  Experience with machine learning model optimization, quantization (including sub-8-bit and quantization-aware training), and deployment on resource-constrained devices 
-  Rigorous experimental design and statistical evaluation skills, including handling class imbalance and reporting variance across runs 
-  Familiarity with embedded ML libraries (e.g., TensorFlow Lite for Microcontrollers, CMSIS-NN) and microcontroller platforms 
-  Ability to establish strong relationships with key stakeholders critical to success, both internally and externally 
-  Strong verbal and written communication skills to audiences of varied background 
-  Ability to simplify complex problems and navigate uncertainty 
-  Ability to quickly ramp on new systems and processes 
-  Demonstrated strong interpersonal, analytical and problem-solving skills 
-  Ability to work in teams and collaborate effectively with people in different functions 
-  Ability to take the initiative and drive for results 
-  Strong time management skills that enable on-time project delivery 

About Us

Why TI?



- The future starts here. As a TIer, you'll play a critical role in defining the next era of semiconductor technology and help create the innovations that shape the world around us.
- Surround yourself with a team of innovators who value your unique perspective and will challenge you to bring your best self to work every day. We believe that fostering a culture of collaboration fuels both personal growth and technological breakthroughs. Explore our company culture .
- At TI, your success goes beyond your work. Take advantage of comprehensive benefits designed to support your total well-being at work and in life, from competitive compensation to extensive health coverage and wellness programs. Learn more about our benefits offerings .

About Texas Instruments

Texas Instruments Incorporated (Nasdaq: TXN) is a global semiconductor company that designs, manufactures and sells analog and embedded processing chips for markets such as industrial, automotive, data center, personal electronics and communications equipment. At our core, we have a passion to create a better world by making electronics more affordable through semiconductors. This passion is alive today as each generation of innovation builds upon the last to make our technology more reliable, more affordable and lower power, making it possible for semiconductors to go into electronics everywhere. role: Systems Engineering Intern (Robotics and AI) at Kilby Labs
jd:
Job Description

Change the world. Love your job.

This Systems Engineering Intern role is within Kilby Labs, the central R&D organization of Texas Instruments (TI). The lab is chartered to develop novel and innovative technologies and strategies for new business opportunities, drive next generation, differentiated technologies for existing businesses and recruit top technical talent for TI.

Role

In this summer Systems Engineering intern role, you will explore AI-enabled control for robotic hands, with a focus on learning policies for reliable grasping and adaptive grip. You will train and evaluate policies in simulation, test them on robotic hand hardware, and help close the gap between the two. What you will do:



-  Research and implement reinforcement learning (RL) and other learning-based policies for robotic grasping. 
-  Develop simulation environments to train and evaluate policies for multi-finger robotic hands. 
-  Use tactile and joint feedback to adapt grip to different objects and disturbances, such as slip. 
-  Benchmark learned policies against conventional control techniques. 

Responsibilities



-  Policy Learning: Design, train and tune control policies for grasping, grip force control and coordinated finger motion. 
-  Simulation: Build and calibrate physics-based models of robotic hands and contact to train and validate policies. 
-  Hardware Validation: Deploy policies on robotic hand prototypes, analyze test data, and resolve differences between simulation and hardware results. 
-  Prototyping: Work with team members on hardware setup, mechanism improvements and test fixtures. 
-  Communication: Document methods and results, share findings with the team, and contribute to patents and publications. 

Qualifications

Minimum Requirements



-  Currently pursuing PhD degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Robotics or related field with a background in reinforcement learning, robot learning or control 
-  Cumulative 3.0/4.0 GPA or higher

-  Strong foundation in reinforcement learning, imitation learning or control theory. 
-  Experience with robotics physics simulators (e.g. MuJoCo, Isaac Lab, PyBullet).
